rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern non-Islamic theories reducing matter to force and force to spirit reproduce the philosophers’ doctrine of immaterial substances; treating such entities as conceptual aligns with theologians.
rows.anchor: Zamanımızda gayr-i İslâmî felsefelerin maddeyi kuvvete, kuvveti rûha ircâ‘eden nazariyeleri de esasında hukemânın sâlifu’z-zikr cevâhir-i mücerrede nazariyesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the material cosmos is one heaven and other heavens exist beyond it, the reality and stations of angels extend to inconceivable heights and depths.
rows.anchor: Bâlâda beyan olunan kavl-i muhtâr vechile bütün kâinât-ı mâddiye bir semâ olduğuna ve bunlardan mâ‘adâ semâlar bulunduğuna göre, hakīkat-i melâikenin ve bunların makamlarının ne kadar yüksekliklere ve derinliklere varacağını tasavvur etmelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says heaven groans rightly because every space the size of a footstep contains an angel prostrating or bowing.
rows.anchor: Semâ gıcırdamaktadır. Ve gıcırdamak hakkıdır. Onda bir kadem mevzi‘i yoktur ki bunda bir melek-i sâcid veya râki‘bulunmasın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report gives successively immense ratios among humans, jinn, land and sea animals, angels of earth, and angels of successive heavens.
rows.anchor: Benî Âdem cinnin öşrü, bunlar hayvânât-ı berriyenin öşrü, hepsi tuyûrun öşrü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narration says all these angels are tiny beside those circling the Throne; the hosts of the Preserved Tablet and Gabriel are countless, and only God knows their kinds, lifetimes, and worship.
rows.anchor: Sonra bunların mecmû‘u Arş etrafında dönen melâikeye karşı denizden bir katre kalır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic ascent report describes battlement-like angels; Gabriel has seen them since his creation but never the same one twice, and one angel says God created 400,000 stars in its lifetime.
rows.anchor: “Bunlar nereye gidiyorlar?” diye Resûlullah Cebrâil’e sordu, Cebrâil “bilmiyorum, ancak yaratıldığımdan beri ben bunları görürüm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These accounts exceed contemporary astronomy; subtle ether bodies cannot explain all angels, at most earthly and lowest-heaven angels unless the lowest heaven is narrowly construed, unlike theologians’ preferred view.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki bu tenvîrât asr-ı hâzırdaki hey’et fikrinden de çok yüksektir ve bunların hepsini ecsâm-ı lâtîfe-i esîriye ile tahdid etmek de pek muvâfık olmasa gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view restricts the angels addressed here to angels of earth, transmitted by al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: Bundan murad melâike-i arzdır diyenler olmuştur ki bu da Dahhâk’in İbn Abbas radıyallahu ‘anhümâ’dan bir rivayetine müntehî olmaktadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Companions and Successors understand all angels, since the wording is general and has no qualifier.
rows.anchor: Lâkin ekser sahâbe ve tâbiîn rıdvânullahi ‘aleyhim ecmaîn hazarâtı lafzın umûmuna ve muhassıs bulunmadığına mebnî bütün melâike olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ question follows their being told the primordial decree concerning succession on earth; God answers that He knows what they do not.
rows.anchor: İşte bütün melâike arzda hilâfete müte‘allik böyle bir takdîr-i ezelînin kendilerine teblîği üzerine hitâb-ı ilâhî karşısında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although angels know generally that God’s knowledge surpasses theirs, His emphatic ‘I indeed’ signals a specific hidden matter: the wisdom and fitness of succession that prompted their wonder at evil.
rows.anchor: makām-ı inkârda tekid ifade eden إِنِّى ile takviye ederek Cenâb-ı Allah’ın bunu tekrar ihbar etmesi gösterir ki murâd-ı ilâhî bu umum içinde bir husûsu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer says angels do not know the wisdom, motives, and fitness of caliphate; it also implies angelic qualities alone are insufficient and that requesting office is improper.
rows.anchor: hilâfetin hikmet ve devâ‘îsi ve ona liyâkat meselesi hakkında bilmediğiniz cihetler var.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the maxim that a person seeking judicial office should not be appointed to it.
rows.anchor: ‘adem-i kifayetine ve talebin ‘adem-i cevâzına da zımnen işaret buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent view is that God coined the names and inscribed or inspired them in Adam; another possibility is that Adam received a special capacity to coin and use names as needed.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan da Âdem’e bütün o isimleri tâlim etti. Ya o esmâyı Allah kendi vaz‘edip Âdem’in rûhuna nakş u ilham etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam did not learn every primordial word instantaneously; he learned language gradually through an endowed capacity under nurture.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âdem’in asl-ı lisân olan isimleri birdenbire bir i‘lâm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s attributes represent humanity’s original nature: as the first human, he transmitted the species’ essential faculties to humankind.
rows.anchor: nev‘-i beşerin mâhiyet ve fıtrat-ı ûlâsı demektir. Zira Âdem nev‘in ilk ferdidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exegetical question is whether ‘all’ means every name or a defined set, and whether the article marks exhaustive generality or a known set.
rows.anchor: Bu isimler nedir ve كُلَّهَا istiğrâkının derece-i şümûlü ne kadardır?

rows.speaker: ضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One universal-names view says Adam learned names used for human understanding, including people, animals, earth, sea, mountains, and donkeys.
rows.anchor:
cebel, himar vesâire hepsi (İbn Ab-
bas’tan Dahhâk)

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid says Adam learned the names of the crow, dove, and everything.
rows.anchor: gurab, hamame ve her şeyin ismi (Mücâhid)

rows.speaker: Saîd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr says Adam learned every name, down to camel, cow, and sheep.
rows.anchor: her şeyin ismi, ba‘îr, bakara, şâte varıncaya kadar (Saîd b. Cübeyr)

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas’tan Saîd b. Ma‘bed
rows.claim: Sa‘id ibn Ma‘bad’s report from Ibn Abbas extends the names to demonstratives such as ‘this’ and ‘that’ and even ‘hadath.’
rows.anchor:
“şu”, “bu”, “hades” bile (İbn Abbas’tan Saîd b. Ma‘-
bed)

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatada says Adam learned names and classes of created kinds, identifying things as ‘this mountain’ or ‘this sea’ and describing their properties.
rows.anchor: her sınıf halkın ismi ve cinsine ircâ‘ı, “şu cebel”, “bu deniz”, “şu şöyle” diye her şeyin ismi (Katâde)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal view amounts to the vocabularies underlying all languages; some extend it to names of everything that would exist through the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Bunların hâsılı, bütün elsinenin aslı olan lügātın hepsi oluyor

rows.speaker: Rebî‘ ve daha diğerleri
rows.claim: Another interpretation restricts the names to those of the angels.
rows.anchor: Melâikenin esâmîsi (Rebî‘ve daha diğerleri)

rows.speaker: İbn Zeyd
rows.claim: A third interpretation says the names are those of Adam’s descendants; Ibn Wahb, Yunus ibn Abd al-A‘la, and others also transmit this view.
rows.anchor: 3. Zürriyetinin esâmîsi (İbn Zeyd’den

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘them’ points to rational beings and favors descendants’ names; some exegetes combine descendants and angels, while the pronoun also rules out God’s names.
rows.anchor: bu kârineye nazaran bazı müfessirîn hem esmâ-i melâikeye ve hem esmâ-i zürriyete şümûlünü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the names as properties of things or mental forms assembled from them, which would be knowledge or inner speech rather than ordinary language.
rows.anchor: Esmâdan murad lisan değil, havâss-ı eşyâ, ta‘bîr-i âharla o havâstan müteşekkil suver-i ilmiyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is certain is that Adam received language teaching and was endowed with knowledge and speech; language matters to the caliphate.
rows.anchor: burada kat‘î olan nokta Hazret-i Âdem’e az veya çok ta’lîm-i lisân edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human linguistic diversity and development owe their foundation to Adam’s innate naming capacity, while knowledge and logic belong essentially to human nature.
rows.anchor: İlim ve mantık hâssası bu suretle nev‘-i insânînin fıtrat-ı asliyesinde dâhil zâtiyyâttan bulunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech is part of the human spirit’s essence; Adam became fully human through knowledge and speech, and language is not merely incidental.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle kuvve-i kelâmiye rûh-i insânînin mâhiyetinden bir cüz teşkil etmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects those who define human essence by sin while treating knowledge and speech as accidents, saying they misunderstand humanity.
rows.anchor: Masiyeti insanın zâtîsi sayıp da sıfat-ı ilmi ve sıfat-ı kelâmı araziyyâttan saymak isteyenler insanı bilememişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If teaching preceded the breathing of spirit, Adam received speech and naming capacity and coined names gradually by divine enablement; if concurrent or later, God taught names gradually by inspiration or necessary knowledge.
rows.anchor: veya sonra ise vâzı‘-ı esmâ, Allah teâlâ’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These alternatives correspond to the legal-theoretical dispute about the origin of language; the apparent reading is actual teaching and its prior determination.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînce tâlim böyle iki suretle de tevil edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Language is the cause of Adam’s appointment as caliph, not its result.
rows.anchor: Yani lisan, Âdem’in eser-i hilâfeti değil, sebeb-i hilâfetidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘them’ is grammatically marked for rational beings, favoring descendants as referents; all names may have been taught while only these referents were presented.
rows.anchor: arz olunan şeylerin zevi’l-‘ukūl olduğunu göstermekte zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent referents are descendants who would succeed Adam, though this seems difficult because Eve and the descendants were not yet created in the narrative.
rows.anchor: en zâhir mâna bu müsemmeyâtın Hazret-i Âdem’e halef olacak olan zürriyetleri olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A well-known hadith explains that descendants were shown to angels as tiny particles, fine ants, or microbes; ‘descendants’ derives from ‘particles.’
rows.anchor: karıncalar, mikroplar misâlinde arz edilmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith implies all future humanity existed in Adam as seedlike particles representing his descendants.
rows.anchor: Bu hadis bunların o zaman Âdem’de henüz tohum hâlinde, yani istikbalde bütün Benî Âdem’i temsil eden ilk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, before earthly descent Adam’s rational soul or subtle ethereal body could contain successive descendant forms; their presentation would then be intellectual, not sensory.
rows.anchor: Bu surette melâikeye arz, arz-ı hissî değil, arz-ı ilmî ve hakīkī olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true referents of names are cognitive forms; Adam received knowledge especially of descendants as well as their names and linguistic forms, which angels lacked.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-vâki‘isimlerin asıl medlûlâtı eşyânın suver-i ilmiyesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This discussion raises whether knowledge is innate or acquired, a question he will explain elsewhere.
rows.anchor: Burada bilfiil ilmin fıtriyeti veya ‘adem-i fıtriyeti meselesi vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s challenge tests angels’ implied claim to succession by asking them to identify the beings and their names if they are correct.
rows.anchor: haydi siz bi’l-işâre ifade etmek istediğiniz hilâfete liyâkatiniz îmasında sâdık yani musîb iseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Administration and justice require knowing subjects, their capacities and rights, and identifying them by name even when absent.
rows.anchor: tasarruf, tedbir, ikāme-i ma‘delet bunların müte‘allaklarını, isti‘dadlarının mertebelerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech and truthful articulation have distinctive intrinsic value beyond knowledge, and legal rulings cannot be carried out without them.
rows.anchor: sıfat-ı ilimden daha fazla bir hususiyet ve meziyet ifade eden sıfat-ı kelâmın, kuvve-i lisâniyenin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God, say they know only what He taught them, and affirm that He is all-knowing and wise.
rows.anchor: Sübhâneke, en yüksek tesbih ve tenzih sana yâ Rab! Senin bize bildirdiğinden başka bizim hiçbir ilmimiz yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Subhan’ is a proper name for glorification, while ‘Subhanaka’ commonly prefaces repentance.
rows.anchor: “Sübhân”, tesbîhin bir ism-i ‘alemidir. “Sübhâneke” de ekseriya tevbe mukaddimesi olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels knew no names, would they lack speech entirely and how could they speak? If they only lacked new names, that alone would not prove they were unfit for succession.
rows.anchor: Melâike hiçbir isim bilmiyorlarsa o zaman sıfat-ı kelâmdan külliyen mahrum bulunuyorlardı demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the names mean all names, angels lack speech; if they mean descendants’ names, that need not prevent speech, so another wisdom must explain their lack of fitness.
rows.anchor: eğer esmâ-i zürriyet ise, diğer esmâyı men‘etmeyeceğinden sıfat-ı kelâma mâni‘olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In either interpretation, God’s communication with angels should be understood as knowledge rather than ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: her iki takdirde melâike ile olan muhâtaba-i ilâhiye sıfat-ı kelâma râci‘olmayıp mânası büsbütün başka olmak ve sıfat-ı ilim ile tevil edilmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels learn names through Adam’s report; knowledge is direct disclosure of reality, while speech conveys it indirectly through signs or deputies.
rows.anchor: kelâm-ı Âdem’in inbâsıyla öğreneceklerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is a direct manifestation of reality; speech is its derivative manifestation through an indicator or sign.
rows.anchor: asıl ilim hakikatin bizzat bir tecellîsi ve bir inkişâf-ı mahsûsudur. Kelâm da ilmin bir tecellîsi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name is a thing, but is a name by serving as a sign or proof that brings something else to mind.
rows.anchor: İsimde kelâmda ise o vechin ancak bir nâibi vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Caliphate suits the representative role of names and speech, first bestowed on Adam; human sciences depend on derivative verbal forms and therefore contain shadowlike concepts.
rows.anchor: hilâfete liyâkat, esmâ ve kelâmdaki bu ma‘nâ-yı niyâbet ile mütenâsib olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s first address to angels was direct knowledge of reality without named or representative forms; their dialogue, glorification, and sanctification likewise express direct illumination.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah ile melâikenin evvelki muhâtabaları hiçbir suver-i ismiye ve niyâbiye karışmayan ve bizzat vech-i hakīkat üzerinde vâki‘olan bir cereyân-ı ilmîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels may lack knowledge or have deficiencies, but do not err or fall into compounded ignorance; they act on revealed text, while humans infer and analogize.
rows.anchor: meleklerin bilmedikleri ve bildiklerinde noksanları bulunabilirse de hataları, cehl-i mürekkebleri olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels did not explicitly claim fitness for succession; they saw the new matter incompletely yet spoke a partial truth without grasping representation’s deeper nature.
rows.anchor: Bâlâdaki ifadelerinde de sarâhaten liyâkat dava etmemişler ve yeni âgâh oldukları meseleyi nâkıs olarak görebilmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human susceptibility to error and compounded ignorance is tied to speech’s representative nature, through which Satan can mislead.
rows.anchor: Beşeriyetin hata ve cehl-i mürekkeb kabiliyeti de kendilerindeki kelâm sıfatı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech is essentially ordered to truth, yet incidental effects can make it false; people may identify words with knowledge and truth and mistake concepts for reality.
rows.anchor: Gerçi kelâm esasen ilm-i hakka ve sıdka mevzû‘dur ve onun nâibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When representation is treated as original and people stop seeking truth beyond it, human evil begins.
rows.anchor: Haslet-i niyâbet, bir asalet telakkī edilir. Ve o zaman insanlığın bütün şerr ü fesâdı başlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Adam both knowledge and speech, taught him the names, and tested his fitness before the angels.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak fıtrat-ı Âdem’i kendi sıfâtından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Adam to report the names to the angels, thereby indicating who will be caliph.
rows.anchor: Melâike i‘tirâf-ı acz ve teslîm-i

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic derivations from ‘udma’ or ‘earth’s surface’ are reported, but the preferred view of Zamakhshari, Baydawi, and Abu al-Su‘ud is a non-Arabic origin on the fa‘al pattern.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî, Beyzâvî, Ebussuud vesâire gibi muhakkikīnin muhtârı budur.

rows.speaker: İmam Şa‘bî
rows.claim: Imam Sha‘bi holds that Adam is Hebrew, like Azer or A‘zar, and says Syriac ‘adam’ means soil.
rows.anchor: İmam Şa‘bî bunun “Âzer”[^78] ve “A‘zar”[^79]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some derive Adam from Syriac ‘hatam,’ which would make the Turkish pronunciation ‘adam’ more original.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da bunun aslı “hâtam” vezninde Süryânî olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether Arabic or foreign, Adam is certainly a proper name rather than a generic noun and is indeclinable for its grammatical reasons.
rows.anchor: Ve her iki takdirde bir ism-i cins olmayıp ism-i ‘alem olduğu muhakkaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Used generically like ‘human’ or ‘person,’ Adam has plural ‘avadim’ and a declinable singular meaning one Adamite; generic nouns begin by generalizing a proper name, and singularity precedes multitude.
rows.anchor: “Âdem”; “beşer”, “insan” gibi ism-i cins makamında kullanılacak olursa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hebrew and Syriac have variant forms; Sabaean ‘Aadhimun’ seems related, and Adam is said to have different names among peoples.
rows.anchor: Her hâlde Arabîden mâ‘adâ İbrânî ve Süryânîde bu ismin muhtelif lehçeleri mevcut olduğu anlaşılıyor.

rows.speaker: Şehristânî
rows.claim: Shahrastani says a Magian Kuyumers tradition identifies Kayumers as Adam; Indian and Persian histories also report this, though other historians disagree.
rows.anchor: Şehristânî’nin Milel ü Nihâl’de beyânına göre Mecûstan Küyumresiye taifesi “Keyûmers Âdem’dir” derler.

rows.speaker: İbnü’l-Esîr
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir records in al-Kamil that the Magians call Jeyumers Adam.
rows.anchor: İbnü’l-Esîr dahi Kâmil’inde “Mecûsun Ceyumers dediği Hazret-i Âdem’dir” diye zikreder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent view is that Adam is a word belonging to humanity’s first language.
rows.anchor: En zâhiri, Âdem ismi beşerin ilk lisânına ait bir kelime olmak üzere ahz edilmek iktizâ edecektir.
